segments.text: Good afternoon, and welcome to the Microsoft fourth quarter fiscal 2026 earnings conference call. All lines have been placed on mute to prevent background noise. I will now turn the call over to Dana Whitfield, Head of Investor Relations.

Thank you, Ryan. On the call today are Marcus Bell, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, and Ellen Park, Chief Financial Officer. Our remarks today include forward-looking statements, which involve risks and uncertainties. Marcus, over to you.

Thank you, Dana. We closed the fiscal year with strong momentum: total revenue of 76.4 billion dollars, up 18 percent year over year, and cloud revenue surpassed 45 billion dollars for the first time as customers continue to consolidate workloads onto our platform.

Thanks, Marcus. Operating income grew 21 percent to 34.9 billion dollars, and earnings per share came in at 3.42 dollars, ahead of our guidance range. Capital expenditures were 24.1 billion dollars in the quarter as we added data-center capacity to meet AI demand.
Management's prepared remarks are now complete. We will now open the lines for questions. Our first question comes from Tom Okafor with Beacon Hill Research. Please go ahead.
Thank you. Ellen, can you talk about supply constraints for accelerators and how dependent the capacity build remains on $NVDA allocations versus your own custom silicon ramp?

We are adding capacity across every layer of the stack, Tom, and our custom silicon program gives us more flexibility in how we serve inference demand. We expect supply and demand to come into better balance as we move through the coming fiscal year.
That concludes today's call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
